title: Trump’s Escalating War With Higher Education

sentences.zh: 我凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.zh: 七十年的太空探索。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: In recent weeks, the Trump administration has put the American university system on notice.
sentences.zh: 最近几周，特朗普政府向美国大学系统发出了警告。

sentences.en: It's pressed for changes, launched investigations, and in some cases, it's even withheld critical funds.
sentences.zh: 它施压要求变革，发起调查，在某些情况下，甚至扣留了关键资金。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Ellen Blinder on how schools are responding to all of this pressure and what it might mean for the future of higher education.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事艾伦·布林德将探讨学校如何应对所有这些压力，以及这对高等教育的未来意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's Monday, March 24th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月24日，星期一。

sentences.en: Ellen, thank you so much for being with us.
sentences.zh: 艾伦，非常感谢你接受我们的采访。

sentences.en: I am not surprised given the news cycle recently and how much we've been hearing about universities that you're working on a Sunday.
sentences.zh: 考虑到最近的新闻周期，以及我们听到那么多关于大学的消息，你周日还在工作，我一点也不惊讶。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: It really feels like we cannot go more than a few days without hearing about this escalating conflict between the Trump administration and the country's colleges and universities.
sentences.zh: 真的感觉我们没过几天就会听到关于特朗普政府与全国高校之间不断升级的冲突的消息。

sentences.en: And you, Ellen, have been covering higher education for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 艾伦，你报道高等教育领域已经很长时间了。

sentences.en: So we thought you'd be the right person to sit down with so that you could kind of break all of this down for us.
sentences.zh: 所以我们认为你是最适合坐下来为我们梳理这一切的人选。

sentences.en: But I think the first thing I want to do is just get a sense from you of whether you've ever seen anything like this showdown
sentences.zh: 但我认为我首先想了解的是，你是否见过类似这样的对峙，

sentences.en: that we are currently seeing between the higher education in this country and the White House.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们目前看到的这个国家的高等教育机构与白宫之间的对峙。

sentences.en: I haven't seen anything like it, but more to the point, a lot of the sources I talk to,
sentences.zh: 我没见过类似的情况，但更重要的是，我交谈过的许多消息来源，

sentences.en: a lot of presidents and chancellors and provosts, people who have been in and around higher education for decades, haven't seen anything like it either.
sentences.zh: 许多校长、院长和教务长，那些在高等教育领域工作了几十年的人，也从未见过这样的情况。

sentences.en: They're almost shell-shocked about what's happening.
sentences.zh: 他们对正在发生的事情几乎感到震惊。

sentences.en: It's been this wave of campaigns against higher education.
sentences.zh: 这已经演变成了一波针对高等教育的运动。

sentences.en: It's been this wave of complicating factors that may or may not have to do with universities themselves.
sentences.zh: 这一波复杂的因素可能与大学本身有关，也可能无关。

sentences.en: And in the end, you've got this real mess for higher education at this point that has left a lot of the country's most elite universities,
sentences.zh: 最终，高等教育陷入了真正的混乱，这让该国许多最顶尖的大学，

sentences.en: but also schools that are less prominent on defense.
sentences.zh: 以及一些不太知名的学校都处于防御状态。

sentences.en: And within all of that, it feels like your reporting has really focused on Columbia University for good reason.
sentences.zh: 在所有这些情况中，感觉你的报道确实集中在哥伦比亚大学，这是有充分理由的。

sentences.en: Columbia has been a poster child for a lot of this conflict and a little bit of a case study, right?
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚大学一直是这场冲突的典型代表，也算是一个案例研究，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, look, it's been a very long year and a half or so for a lot of higher education,
sentences.zh: 我是说，你看，对于许多高等教育机构来说，过去一年半左右的时间非常漫长，

sentences.en: but you will not find many universities in this country that have had a longer year and a half than Columbia.
sentences.zh: 但你在这个国家找不到几所大学比哥伦比亚大学度过的这一年半更艰难了。

sentences.en: It has absolutely morphed into being a poster child for crackdowns and protests and really bitter disputes about what a university can and should be.
sentences.zh: 它已经完全变成了镇压、抗议以及关于大学能够且应该是什么样子的激烈争论的代名词。

sentences.en: And that's really been coming home to roost these last couple of weeks.
sentences.zh: 而这在过去几周里真正产生了后果。

sentences.en: Let's dive into Columbia a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 让我们更深入地了解一下哥伦比亚大学的情况。

sentences.en: Can you just walk us through what's been happening there?
sentences.zh: 你能带我们梳理一下那里发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Well, Columbia has really been one of the biggest hubs of campus protests since the war in Gaza erupted and since the Hamas attack on Israel in October of 23.
sentences.zh: 嗯，自加沙战争爆发以及23年10月哈马斯袭击以色列以来，哥伦比亚大学确实一直是校园抗议活动最大的中心之一。

sentences.en: Columbia had one of the most prolific encampments last spring.
sentences.zh: 去年春天，哥伦比亚大学出现了最激烈的营地抗议活动之一。

sentences.en: Its university president at the time went to Capitol Hill, had a pretty roundly criticized appearance there.
sentences.zh: 当时的大学校长去了国会山，在那里表现得相当糟糕，受到了广泛批评。

sentences.en: And what was interesting about Columbia is that a lot of people thought the university was getting it wrong.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚大学有趣的地方在于，很多人认为这所大学的处理方式是错误的。

sentences.en: It wasn't just one side or the other that thought the university was blowing it.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是某一方认为大学搞砸了。

sentences.en: And so as time has gone on, Columbia has really been, you know, a synonym for college chaos essentially over the last year and a half.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，在过去一年半里，哥伦比亚大学实际上已经成了大学混乱的代名词。

sentences.en: Right, and that chaos has caused a lot of people on all sides to say that the university, as you put it, is blowing it.
sentences.zh: 没错，这种混乱导致各方人士都说，正如你所言，这所大学搞砸了。

sentences.en: Can you just describe a little bit what do they mean by blowing it exactly?
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下他们所说的“搞砸了”到底是什么意思吗？

sentences.en: Well, the left felt that Columbia was essentially becoming a police state and that it was being far too aggressive in tamping down on protest,
sentences.zh: 嗯，左派认为哥伦比亚大学本质上正在变成一个警察国家，在镇压抗议方面表现得过于激进，

sentences.en: on looking to restrict academic freedom.
sentences.zh: 并且试图限制学术自由。

sentences.en: They essentially saw a university that was crumpling under pressure from the right wing.
sentences.zh: 他们本质上看到的是一所屈服于右翼压力的大学。

sentences.en: The right had plenty of complaints of its own.
sentences.zh: 右翼也有很多自己的抱怨。

sentences.en: The right was mostly concerned that Columbia had descended into, you know, becoming this hot house of anti-Semitism,
sentences.zh: 右翼主要担心的是哥伦比亚大学已经沦落为反犹太主义的温床，

sentences.en: that it had allowed campus protests to just run amok and make one of the country's most prominent universities, this kind of lawless environment.
sentences.zh: 它允许校园抗议活动肆无忌惮，使这所全国最著名的大学变成了这种无法无天的环境。

sentences.en: And that has been a drum that Republicans have been beating at this point for many, many months.
sentences.zh: 这正是共和党人几个月来一直敲打的鼓点。

sentences.en: And it's one President Trump and his allies were happy to jump on during the campaign and then as soon as they returned to power in January.
sentences.zh: 这也是特朗普总统及其盟友在竞选期间，以及一月份重掌权力后乐于利用的话题。

sentences.en: And when they returned to power, what were they saying about universities?
sentences.zh: 当他们重掌权力时，他们对大学说了些什么？

sentences.en: It's very clear from the get-go that rooting out anti-Semitism on campuses is now going to go from being a campaign talking point to a real focus of the federal government.
sentences.zh: 从一开始就很清楚，根除校园反犹太主义将从竞选口号转变为联邦政府的真正重点。

sentences.en: So we start seeing executive orders and decisions that really start to shape how this is all going to play out.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始看到行政命令和决策，这些开始真正塑造这一切将如何发展。

sentences.en: One of the most important things we saw was this idea that the Department of Justice was starting investigating and visiting 10 universities that they saw as really having a lot of problems with anti-Semitism in their view.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的最重要的事情之一是司法部开始调查并走访了10所他们认为在反犹太主义方面存在严重问题的大学。

sentences.en: Columbia was on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚大学就在名单上。

sentences.en: And what are these investigations?
sentences.zh: 这些调查是什么？

sentences.en: Tell us about those.
sentences.zh: 跟我们说说这些调查吧。

sentences.en: Well, they got a whole range of investigations.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们进行了一系列调查。

sentences.en: There's this Department of Justice investigation that looks at whether Columbia and other schools were essentially allowing anti-Semitism to take hold and it was unlawful discrimination.
sentences.zh: 司法部的调查旨在查看哥伦比亚大学和其他学校是否本质上允许反犹太主义扎根，这构成了非法歧视。

sentences.en: You've got an investigation from the Department of Education's Office of Civil Rights that's looking at the same types of things.
sentences.zh: 教育部民权办公室也在进行调查，查看同样类型的问题。

sentences.en: You've got, you know, investigators from the Department of Health and Human Services talking about universities.
sentences.zh: 还有卫生与公众服务部的调查人员在谈论大学问题。

sentences.en: And it's coming from everywhere.
sentences.zh: 而且这种压力来自四面八方。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, they are covering the waterfront on just about everything you can imagine.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，他们几乎涵盖了你能想象到的所有方面。

sentences.en: And Columbia was an easy target.
sentences.zh: 而哥伦比亚大学是一个容易攻击的目标。

sentences.en: So these investigations tend to take a very long time,
sentences.zh: 所以这些调查往往需要很长时间，

sentences.en: but it becomes very clear very quickly that the federal government is going to be moving at really warp speed when it comes to these universities.
sentences.zh: 但很快就会变得非常清楚，联邦政府在对待这些大学时将以极快的速度采取行动。

sentences.en: And on March 7th, the government tells Columbia that it's going to withhold about $400 million in grants and contracts to the university.
sentences.zh: 3月7日，政府告诉哥伦比亚大学，将扣留该大学约4亿美元的拨款和合同资金。

sentences.en: $400 million sounds like a ton of money.
sentences.zh: 4亿美元听起来是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: But how much does that actually matter for Columbia, which is obviously an enormous institution?
sentences.zh: 但对于哥伦比亚大学这样显然规模巨大的机构来说，这到底有多重要？

sentences.en: So a $400 million cut would be a lot at any college or university in this country.
sentences.zh: 所以，4亿美元的削减对这个国家的任何学院或大学来说都是巨大的。

sentences.en: But Columbia, to put it in perspective, has like $6.6 billion in annual revenues.
sentences.zh: 但从宏观来看，哥伦比亚大学每年的收入约为66亿美元。

sentences.en: And government grants and contracts make up about 20% of its revenue.
sentences.zh: 政府拨款和合同约占其收入的20%。

sentences.en: So when the word came down from Washington about this $400 million cut, Columbia's interim president, she's a doctor named Katrina Armstrong,
sentences.zh: 所以当华盛顿传来削减这4亿美元的消息时，哥伦比亚大学的临时校长，一位名叫卡特里娜·阿姆斯特朗的医生，

sentences.en: she said a cut of the size would be felt pretty much all over the campus.
sentences.zh: 她说这种规模的削减几乎会在整个校园感受到。

sentences.en: It wouldn't just be in one lab or one academic department or the hospital.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是在某个实验室、某个学术部门或医院。

sentences.en: It was the kind of cut that was just going to shake the campus really to its core.
sentences.zh: 这种削减足以从根本上撼动整个校园。

sentences.en: So what's Columbia supposed to do about this then?
sentences.zh: 那么哥伦比亚大学对此该怎么办呢？

sentences.en: What can it even do?
sentences.zh: 它还能做什么？

sentences.en: Well, that's an interesting question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: But they got something of an answer a few days later when the federal government sent another letter to Columbia.
sentences.zh: 但几天后，当联邦政府给哥伦比亚大学发了另一封信时，他们得到了一些答案。

sentences.en: And this letter essentially was a ransom note, as some people have put it.
sentences.zh: 正如一些人所说，这封信本质上是一封勒索信。

sentences.en: It was a letter that spelled out a list of demands for Columbia to meet if it wanted to start a conversation with the federal government about restoring that $400 million in funding.
sentences.zh: 这是一封列出了哥伦比亚大学必须满足的要求清单的信，如果它想开始与联邦政府对话以恢复那4亿美元的资金的话。

sentences.en: And what were those demands?
sentences.zh: 那么这些要求是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the demands kind of ran the gamut.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些要求五花八门。

sentences.en: They were everything from having the university adopt a formal definition of anti-Semitism.
sentences.zh: 从要求大学采用反犹太主义的正式定义，应有尽有。

sentences.en: There was a push to ban masks on campus because a lot of protesters on campuses have been covering their faces.
sentences.zh: 还有人推动禁止在校园内佩戴口罩，因为许多校园抗议者一直遮住脸。

sentences.en: There was a call to really review the admissions process, to overhaul the disciplinary system, to empower campus security officers with arrest powers.
sentences.zh: 还有呼吁真正审查招生程序，彻底改革纪律处分制度，赋予校园保安人员逮捕权。

sentences.en: And then there was this idea that they should put Columbia's Middle Eastern, South Asian,
sentences.zh: 然后还有一种想法，就是他们应该将哥伦比亚大学的中东、南亚、

sentences.en: and African Studies Department under what the government described as academic receivership.
sentences.zh: 和非洲研究系置于政府所描述的“学术接管”之下。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So some of the things that you outlined sound very extreme and some maybe less so based on my limited knowledge of how universities operate.
sentences.zh: 所以你概述的一些事情听起来非常极端，而基于我对大学运作方式的有限了解，有些可能没那么极端。

sentences.en: How do we interpret some of these demands?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何解读这些要求中的一些？

sentences.en: Some of them were, as you said, kind of mainstream, if you will.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，其中一些算是主流，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: I mean, like the mask ban proposal was pretty well in line with what the University of California system has done.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，比如口罩禁令提案与加州大学系统所做的非常一致。

sentences.en: So that wasn't seen as this totally off-the-wall demand.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不被视为完全离谱的要求。

sentences.en: The idea that you would have security officers with arrest powers, a lot of campus police departments around the country have arrest powers.
sentences.zh: 关于赋予保安人员逮捕权的想法，全国许多校园警察部门都有逮捕权。

sentences.en: It's a somewhat loaded question at a school like Columbia, which has a long history of campus protest and a complicated history with the police.
sentences.zh: 在哥伦比亚大学这样的学校，这是一个相当敏感的问题，因为它有着悠久的校园抗议历史和复杂的警察关系史。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But the one that really got the biggest attention was this idea of academic receivership that really set off alarm bells all over the campus and all over academia.
sentences.zh: 但引起最大关注的是“学术接管”这个想法，它在整个校园和学术界敲响了警钟。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: The reason is because historically, universities, especially private ones, have near absolute control over what they're teaching and how they're running their academic departments.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，从历史上看，大学，尤其是私立大学，对它们的教学内容和学术部门的运作方式拥有近乎绝对的控制权。

sentences.en: So the idea that the federal government would directly or indirectly dictate to a university what its curriculum and teaching should look like, that was a red flag.
sentences.zh: 所以，联邦政府直接或间接地向大学发号施令，规定其课程和教学应该是什么样子，这是一个危险信号。

sentences.en: And one thing to remember, though, is that this letter to Columbia did not arrive in a vacuum.
sentences.zh: 不过要记住的一点是，这封给哥伦比亚大学的信并不是凭空而来的。

sentences.en: This has been months and months of scrutiny on Columbia that's been building.
sentences.zh: 几个月来，哥伦比亚大学一直受到越来越多的审查。

sentences.en: And then these last few weeks, you've even had Immigrations and Customs Enforcement officers on campus.
sentences.zh: 而在过去几周，你甚至看到移民和海关执法局的官员出现在校园里。

sentences.en: You've had a green card holder, Mahmoud Khalil, detained because of his protest activities.
sentences.zh: 一名绿卡持有者马哈茂德·哈利勒因为抗议活动被拘留。

sentences.en: There's been this thread and this implied thread of deporting students and pulling visas.
sentences.zh: 一直存在着驱逐学生和吊销签证的威胁，以及这种隐含的威胁。

sentences.en: And it's really created this challenging environment where Columbia has felt besieged really in every way you could imagine.
sentences.zh: 这确实创造了一个充满挑战的环境，哥伦比亚大学在你能想象到的各个方面都感到被围困。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So obviously, Columbia is under a ton of pressure.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，哥伦比亚大学承受着巨大的压力。

sentences.en: And I would imagine that there was also a lot of pressure from people who did not want the school to cave to the administration's demands.
sentences.zh: 我想，那些不希望学校屈服于政府要求的人也施加了很大的压力。

sentences.en: Oh, there was so much pressure.
sentences.zh: 哦，压力太大了。

sentences.en: Even among people who were frustrated by Columbia over the last year, year and a half, there was fear that Columbia was going to cave to these demands.
sentences.zh: 即使在过去一年、一年半里对哥伦比亚大学感到沮丧的人中，也担心哥伦比亚大学会屈服于这些要求。

sentences.en: The idea that the Trump administration could effectively bully a university into doing something was really alarming to people.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府能够有效地欺凌一所大学去做某事，这让人们感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: And there was this really swelling fear and frustration as Columbia deliberated over what to do.
sentences.zh: 当哥伦比亚大学在考虑该怎么做时，这种恐惧和挫败感确实在不断膨胀。

sentences.en: And on Friday afternoon, we got our answer when Columbia's interim president released a letter.
sentences.zh: 周五下午，我们得到了答案，哥伦比亚大学的临时校长发布了一封信。

sentences.en: And it basically said the university was bowing to the government's demands.
sentences.zh: 信中基本上说大学正在屈服于政府的要求。

sentences.en: So what do you make of the fact that they just kind of caved to everything?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于他们就这样屈服于一切的事实，你怎么看？

sentences.en: Well, Columbia never in its announcement really talked about the $400 million in funding.
sentences.zh: 嗯，哥伦比亚大学在声明中从未真正谈到那4亿美元的资金。

sentences.en: They never made this explicit connection.
sentences.zh: 他们从未明确建立这种联系。

sentences.en: But I think the administration at Columbia felt like it had very little choice in the matter.
sentences.zh: 但我认为哥伦比亚大学的管理层觉得他们在这件事上几乎别无选择。

sentences.en: You know, they could have litigated this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们本可以就此进行诉讼。

sentences.en: There were people who were saying you should go to court, challenge the administration, make them prove their case.
sentences.zh: 有人说你应该诉诸法庭，挑战政府，让他们证明自己的主张。

sentences.en: And Columbia made the calculation that it would agree.
sentences.zh: 而哥伦比亚大学做出了妥协的决定。

sentences.en: Now, some of these things were ideas that Columbia had already been kicking around before the administration sent the letter.
sentences.zh: 现在，其中一些想法是哥伦比亚大学在政府发信之前就已经在考虑的。

sentences.en: But the optics were really bad here.
sentences.zh: 但这里的观感真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: I mean, they were essentially saying we're going to do it in response to a letter from the federal government.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们本质上是在说，我们这样做是为了回应联邦政府的一封信。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It seems like, number one, the administration had Columbia over a barrel from the way that you're describing it.
sentences.zh: 看起来，第一，从你的描述来看，政府确实让哥伦比亚大学陷入了困境。

sentences.en: And number two, that they just decided, like, it is not worth fighting the government.
sentences.zh: 第二，他们只是决定，与政府对抗是不值得的。

sentences.en: There was a calculation that was made that they either could not win this fight, would not win this fight, or it would get worse if they did try to fight it.
sentences.zh: 他们做出了一个计算，认为他们要么无法赢得这场斗争，要么不会赢得这场斗争，或者如果他们真的试图反抗，情况会变得更糟。

sentences.en: And they came down on the side of seeking to settle.
sentences.zh: 他们最终选择了寻求和解。

sentences.en: But here's the kicker of all this.
sentences.zh: 但这是这一切中最关键的一点。

sentences.en: This is the rub.
sentences.zh: 这就是症结所在。

sentences.en: By agreeing to all these concessions, Columbia did not automatically reopen the spigot of $400 million.
sentences.zh: 通过同意所有这些让步，哥伦比亚大学并没有自动重新开启那4亿美元的资金水龙头。

sentences.en: That $400 million does not just automatically return.
sentences.zh: 那4亿美元不会自动退回。

sentences.en: These concessions that Columbia made were essentially their effort to get the government to come to the negotiating table to talk about restoring that $400 million.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚大学做出的这些让步，本质上是他们努力让政府坐到谈判桌前，讨论恢复那4亿美元资金的尝试。

sentences.en: It wasn't even like, do all of this and you'll get your money back.
sentences.zh: 甚至不是说，做完所有这些你就能拿回你的钱。

sentences.en: It was do all of this and maybe we'll talk to you about getting your money back.
sentences.zh: 而是说，做完所有这些，也许我们会和你谈谈拿回钱的事。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So if Columbia gets the money back, there's likely to be a bigger cost than what's already been announced.
sentences.zh: 所以如果哥伦比亚大学把钱退回去，那么付出的代价很可能比已经宣布的还要大。

sentences.en: Right, and that bigger cost, I mean, we've been focusing a lot on Columbia, but there are other schools that the administration has said that it's targeting, right?
sentences.zh: 没错，而且那个更大的代价，我是说，我们一直把目光集中在哥伦比亚大学身上，但政府也说过它还针对其他学校，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, it feels like we should be prepared to see these hardball tactics elsewhere soon.
sentences.zh: 感觉我们应该做好准备，很快就会在其他地方看到这些强硬手段。

sentences.en: You should absolutely be prepared to see those hardball tactics.
sentences.zh: 你绝对应该做好准备看到那些强硬手段。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我是说，

sentences.en: you've got dozens of universities in the first two months of the Trump administration that have been told they are facing an investigation by at least one agency of the federal government.
sentences.zh: 在特朗普政府执政的头两个月里，有几十所大学被告知它们正面临至少一个联邦政府机构的调查。

sentences.en: And they're not even all like Harvard and Columbia.
sentences.zh: 而且它们甚至不全是像哈佛和哥伦比亚大学那样的名校。

sentences.en: Ohio State University is on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 俄亥俄州立大学就在名单上。

sentences.en: The University of Hawaii is on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 夏威夷大学也在名单上。

sentences.en: It's fair to say that the administration seems to be embarking on a coast-to-coast campaign against higher education.
sentences.zh: 可以公平地说，政府似乎正在对高等教育发起一场全国性的运动。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是 Wena Liu。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《Connections》谜题。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是 Sam Mazursky，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由人制作的，就像你们刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: So, Alan, before the break, you told us about some of the fear that these threats and these demands are instilling at not just Columbia,
sentences.zh: 那么，Alan，休息之前，你告诉我们这些威胁和要求不仅在哥伦比亚大学，

sentences.en: but more broadly at universities around the country.
sentences.zh: 而且在全国各地的大学里都引发了一些恐惧。

sentences.en: So can you just tell us a little bit more about what you're hearing about that?
sentences.zh: 你能再多告诉我们一些你所听到的关于这方面的情况吗？

sentences.en: Well, remember, it's not just a matter of will the administration come after my particular university that's driving college presidents nuts right now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，记住，现在让大学校长们抓狂的不仅仅是政府会不会针对我所在的这所特定大学的问题。

sentences.en: The administration is looking at all kinds of budget cuts that could broadly affect higher education.
sentences.zh: 政府正在考虑各种可能广泛影响高等教育的预算削减。

sentences.en: So one of the things we've been seeing the last few weeks is more hiring freezes.
sentences.zh: 所以我们过去几周看到的情况之一是更多的招聘冻结。

sentences.en: We've seen layoffs.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到了裁员。

sentences.en: We've seen schools shutting down laboratories because they're starting to lose grant funding or they're fearing, you know, what's coming next.
sentences.zh: 我们看到学校关闭了实验室，因为它们开始失去拨款，或者担心接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: Columbia is among the most powerful universities in the United States.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚大学是美国最有实力的大学之一。

sentences.en: One of the oldest, one of the richeSt.
sentences.zh: 最古老、最富有的大学之一。

sentences.en: And one of the biggest fears has been that if Columbia University cannot stand up to the federal government for whatever reason, what are other universities supposed to do?
sentences.zh: 最大的恐惧之一是，如果哥伦比亚大学因为某种原因无法顶住联邦政府的压力，其他大学该怎么办？

sentences.en: But just to play devil's advocate for a second here, I think a lot of people listening to this are going to think to themselves, well,
sentences.zh: 但为了反驳一下，我想很多听众会想，嗯，

sentences.en: why should universities get so much money from the federal government, especially the universities that are pretty rich to begin with?
sentences.zh: 为什么大学应该从联邦政府那里得到这么多钱，尤其是那些本来就很富有的大学？

sentences.en: So can you just explain to us, like, why are these two institutions, the federal government and higher education, why are they so intertwined to begin with?
sentences.zh: 所以你能给我们解释一下，为什么这两个机构——联邦政府和高等教育——从一开始就如此紧密相连？

sentences.en: So this country has had higher education since before the signing of the Declaration of Independence.
sentences.zh: 这个国家在《独立宣言》签署之前就已经有了高等教育。

sentences.en: But it wasn't until the late 19th century when Johns Hopkins University was founded as the nation's first research university when you started to see a much more explicit focus on research.
sentences.zh: 但直到19世纪末约翰霍普金斯大学作为全国第一所研究型大学成立时，你才开始看到对研究的更加明确的关注。

sentences.en: That took a little while to take root.
sentences.zh: 这花了一段时间才扎根。

sentences.en: But around World War II is when the universities and the federal government really got to work with each other.
sentences.zh: 但大约在二战时期，大学和联邦政府才真正开始合作。

sentences.en: The country had a lot of wartime needs.
sentences.zh: 国家当时有很多战时需求。

sentences.en: They needed big ideas, innovation.
sentences.zh: 他们需要伟大的想法和创新。

sentences.en: They needed interpreters and translators for these kind of esoteric languages.
sentences.zh: 他们需要这些深奥语言的口译员和翻译员。

sentences.en: And those were the kind of people you could find at universities.
sentences.zh: 而这些人才正是你在大学里能找到的。

sentences.en: And it created this relationship.
sentences.zh: 这建立了一种关系。

sentences.en: The idea was that the universities would get this research funding, it would fuel their labs, it would fuel the scientists,
sentences.zh: 当时的理念是，大学获得研究经费，这会推动实验室的发展，推动科学家的研究，

sentences.en: and then that research would flow into corporate America, it would flow into other parts of the government, other parts of academia.
sentences.zh: 然后这些研究成果会流入美国企业界，流入政府的其他部门，以及学术界的其他领域。

sentences.en: And the result was the country got new pharmaceutical drugs, new technology, Nobel Prize winners come out of university labs in a lot of cases doing federally funded research.
sentences.zh: 结果就是国家获得了新的药物、新技术，很多情况下，诺贝尔奖得主都是从大学实验室里走出来的，他们从事的是联邦资助的研究。

sentences.en: And just to be clear, when we're talking about federal money, we're not just talking about Columbia and the Ivy Leagues, right?
sentences.zh: 顺便明确一下，当我们谈论联邦资金时，我们不仅仅是在谈论哥伦比亚大学和常春藤盟校，对吧？

sentences.en: Can you just give us a sense, how dependent are universities across the board on federal money?
sentences.zh: 你能给我们一个概念吗，各地的大学对联邦资金的依赖程度如何？

sentences.en: Oh, I mean, you have billions and billions of dollars that flow to campuses all over the country.
sentences.zh: 哦，我是说，有数十亿数十亿美元流入全国各地的校园。

sentences.en: You know, you've got the University of Georgia, which, for example, was getting federal funding for a lab that focused on peanuts.
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如佐治亚大学，它就曾获得联邦资助用于一个专注于花生的实验室。

sentences.en: You know, Illinois, they get money for insulin research.
sentences.zh: 你知道，伊利诺伊大学，他们获得了胰岛素研究的资金。

sentences.en: You've had all this money flowing to public universities, private universities, red states, blue states, you know, large, small.
sentences.zh: 所有的这些资金都流向了公立大学、私立大学、红州、蓝州，无论规模大小。

sentences.en: Now, just about every college or university in this country has some kind of financial tie to the federal government.
sentences.zh: 现在，这个国家的几乎每一所学院或大学都与联邦政府有某种财务联系。

sentences.en: Some of them have much larger financial ties than others.
sentences.zh: 有些学校的财务联系比其他学校要大得多。

sentences.en: But when you start talking about cutting research funding, the trickle-down effect is enormous.
sentences.zh: 但当你开始谈论削减研究经费时，其连锁反应是巨大的。

sentences.en: It's not just cutting off Harvard and Yale and the like.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是切断哈佛、耶鲁之类的学校的资金。

sentences.en: It's cutting off, potentially, state universities near you.
sentences.zh: 这可能会切断你附近的州立大学的资金。

sentences.en: That makes sense, but since you mentioned Harvard and Yale, those schools, along with Columbia and Penn and other places,
sentences.zh: 这说得通，但既然你提到了哈佛和耶鲁，那些学校，连同哥伦比亚大学、宾夕法尼亚大学和其他地方，

sentences.en: are schools that have literally billions of dollars in endowments.
sentences.zh: 都是拥有数十亿美元捐赠基金的学校。

sentences.en: And so it feels reasonable to say, OK, for those schools that are sitting on top of these giant piles of money,
sentences.zh: 所以说，好吧，对于那些坐拥巨额资金的学校来说，这似乎是合理的，

sentences.en: they should be able to use their big endowments to pay for their day-to-day operations.
sentences.zh: 他们应该能够利用他们庞大的捐赠基金来支付日常运营费用。

sentences.en: They should not need to rely on the federal government.
sentences.zh: 他们不应该依赖联邦政府。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: But one thing to know about endowments is they tend to have a lot of what are called restricted funds, which really limit what the money can be used for.
sentences.zh: 但关于捐赠基金有一点需要知道，它们往往有很多所谓的限制性资金，这极大地限制了资金的用途。

sentences.en: So, for example, you, Rachel Abrams, might have donated money to a university for a specific topic, a specific job, a specific research project, whatever it might be.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，你，Rachel Abrams，可能为某个特定主题、特定职位、特定研究项目等捐赠了钱给大学。

sentences.en: That money cannot just be used for another project because they suddenly need the money.
sentences.zh: 那笔钱不能因为他们突然需要钱就挪作他用。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You can't just go to the bank and say, I have something I want to research.
sentences.zh: 你不能直接去银行说，我有一些想研究的东西。

sentences.en: Give me $100 million, please.
sentences.zh: 请给我一亿美元。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not just like going to the ATM.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这不像去自动取款机取钱那么简单。

sentences.en: And not only are university officials really handcuffed on what they can do with their endowments,
sentences.zh: 而且大学官员不仅在如何使用捐赠基金方面受到束缚，

sentences.en: there's actually a push among some Republicans in Washington to tax the biggest endowments at even higher levels.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿的一些共和党人实际上还在推动对最大的捐赠基金征收更高的税。

sentences.en: So if that happens, there will be even less money for them to be able to spend on things like research and the like.
sentences.zh: 所以如果这种情况发生，他们能用于研究等方面的资金就会更少。

sentences.en: So when you put all this together, the punitive threats to withhold funding, the broader budget cuts that we're seeing in the name of government efficiency,
sentences.zh: 所以当你把所有这些加在一起，以扣留资金为威胁的惩罚，以政府效率为名看到的更广泛的预算削减，

sentences.en: possible changes to the tax structure for endowments,
sentences.zh: 可能对捐赠基金税收结构的改变，

sentences.en: what we're seeing is potentially a really dramatic realignment of the relationship between the federal government and universities in this country.
sentences.zh: 我们所看到的是这个国家联邦政府与大学之间关系可能发生的非常剧烈的重组。

sentences.en: And what does that new realignment look like and what is driving it?
sentences.zh: 那么这种新的重组是什么样的，又是什么在驱动它呢？

sentences.en: Well, look, there have been frustrations building with higher education for years and actually decades in this country.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你看，这个国家对高等教育的挫败感已经积累了多年，实际上是几十年了。

sentences.en: There's been this idea that they're for the elite, they build the elite, they're too expensive.
sentences.zh: 一直有一种观点认为它们是为精英服务的，它们培养精英，而且太昂贵了。

sentences.en: What is even the point of a college degree?
sentences.zh: 大学学位到底有什么意义？

sentences.en: And you've had this emerging tension between what universities think they should be and what other people in this country think they should be.
sentences.zh: 大学认为自己应该是什么样，而这个国家的其他人认为它们应该是什么样，这两者之间出现了新兴的紧张关系。

sentences.en: You're basically saying that there are two competing visions.
sentences.zh: 你基本上是在说有两种相互竞争的愿景。

sentences.en: And I'm kind of wondering what the divide is here because you had mentioned at one point that some of this tension is ideological.
sentences.zh: 我有点好奇这里的分歧是什么，因为你曾提到这种紧张关系中有一些是意识形态上的。

sentences.en: So is there, for example, a vision that is coming from the left?
sentences.zh: 那么，例如，是否有一种来自左翼的愿景？

sentences.en: Well, I don't think it's just the left.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不认为这仅仅是左翼的问题。

sentences.en: I think universities, especially the big research schools, have really assertive visions for their role in a modern society.
sentences.zh: 我认为大学，尤其是大型研究型学校，对它们在现代社会中的角色有着非常明确的愿景。

sentences.en: They want to be places where they're really, you know, training the great thinkers of the day, talking about the big debates.
sentences.zh: 它们希望成为能够培养当今伟大思想家、讨论重大辩论的地方。

sentences.en: They're doing research that changes the world.
sentences.zh: 它们正在进行改变世界的研究。

sentences.en: There is independence.
sentences.zh: 这里有独立性。

sentences.en: They're extending their missions well beyond their campuses.
sentences.zh: 它们正在将使命扩展到校园之外。

sentences.en: That's their vision.
sentences.zh: 这就是它们的愿景。

sentences.en: Now, there's another school of thought.
sentences.zh: 现在，还有另一种思想流派。

sentences.en: Some of it is politically motivated, that these schools should not be what they are.
sentences.zh: 其中一些是出于政治动机，认为这些学校不应该成为现在的样子。

sentences.en: They should be places where teaching is the focus, where workforce development is the goal,
sentences.zh: 它们应该成为以教学为重点、以劳动力发展为目标的地方，

sentences.en: where you should come out of college with a degree that prepares you for the quote-unquote real world.
sentences.zh: 你应该带着一个能让你为所谓的“现实世界”做好准备的学位从大学毕业。

sentences.en: This school of thought is very stringent on the idea that they don't want universities and colleges to be, you know, ideology factories.
sentences.zh: 这种思想流派非常坚定地认为，他们不希望大学成为意识形态工厂。

sentences.en: If you think through the list of complaints, it's that there's been affirmative action on campuses over the years.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细想想这些抱怨，就会发现多年来校园里一直存在平权行动。

sentences.en: It's that the people up in academia just sneer at the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 学术界的人只是对世界其他地方嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: They don't really want as many, I guess, abstract outcomes.
sentences.zh: 我想他们并不真的想要那么多抽象的成果。

sentences.en: They want concrete things, you know, where you can take a degree and go do X, Y, or Z.
sentences.zh: 他们想要具体的东西，你知道，你可以拿着学位去从事某项具体工作。

sentences.en: Now, this is not a new argument.
sentences.zh: 现在，这并不是一个新论点。

sentences.en: But the reality is that universities have done a generally terrible job of making the case for themselves.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，大学在为自己辩护方面做得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: And why is that exactly?
sentences.zh: 那究竟是为什么呢？

sentences.en: You can probably blame it on a lot of different things.
sentences.zh: 你可能可以把它归咎于很多不同的事情。

sentences.en: Sometimes when they're talking about their research, they go so deep in the weeds, no one understands what the research is about or what it's going to do.
sentences.zh: 有时当他们谈论研究时，他们陷入了太深的细节，没人能理解研究的内容或它将起到什么作用。

sentences.en: They've done a pretty terrible job of explaining how tuition costs work and how financial aid works.
sentences.zh: 他们在解释学费成本如何运作以及经济援助如何运作方面做得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know if the last time you looked at like a financial aid application or a scholarship listing, it's this muck.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不知道你上次看经济援助申请或奖学金列表是什么时候，那简直是一团糟。

sentences.en: It's gobbledygook.
sentences.zh: 全是官话套话。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, look, there's a whole body of research out there that says if you're a college graduate, you are likely to have higher lifetime incomes, less likely to be in poverty.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我是说，你看，有大量的研究表明，如果你是大学毕业生，你终身的收入可能会更高，陷入贫困的可能性更小。

sentences.en: The outcomes tend to be pretty good.
sentences.zh: 结果往往相当不错。

sentences.en: But what they haven't done a good job of is explaining that.
sentences.zh: 但他们没能很好地解释这一点。

sentences.en: For whatever reason, they cannot muster much of a coherent defense.
sentences.zh: 不管出于什么原因，他们无法拿出有力的辩护。

sentences.en: I do wonder if one of the reasons that universities are struggling to make a case for themselves is that they do need to be reformed.
sentences.zh: 我确实想知道，大学难以证明自己价值的原因之一是否是它们确实需要改革。

sentences.en: Like any major institution with a multibillion-dollar budget probably does have some bloat and inefficiencies here and there.
sentences.zh: 就像任何拥有数十亿美元预算的大型机构一样，可能确实存在一些臃肿和低效的地方。

sentences.en: But this conversation does feel connected to wider conversations we've been having recently on the show about government efficiency, like cutting federal agencies, for example.
sentences.zh: 但这次谈话确实感觉与我们最近在节目中讨论的关于政府效率的更广泛话题有关，比如削减联邦机构。

sentences.en: Like, sure, these places could probably be run better, but is it necessary to just gut them wholesale?
sentences.zh: 就像，当然，这些地方可能可以经营得更好，但有必要彻底摧毁它们吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, look, I would be hard-pressed to name a college president who does not think there need to be changes somewhere in the system.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我是说，你看，我很难说出哪位大学校长认为系统不需要在某些地方进行改革。

sentences.en: But I think they are worried about the proverbial throwing out the baby with the bathwater here.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们担心的是这里会出现“倒洗澡水连孩子一起倒掉”的情况。

sentences.en: They will acknowledge for all the flaws of universities, and they will often admit there are flaws, that the system is too much the envy of the world to just trash.
sentences.zh: 他们会承认大学的所有缺陷，而且他们通常也会承认确实存在缺陷，但这个系统太令人羡慕了，不能就这样毁掉。

sentences.en: You know, it really feels like we are in a moment where the kind of existential fear that you described,
sentences.zh: 你知道，真的感觉我们正处于这样一个时刻，你所描述的那种生存恐惧，

sentences.en: it's allowing the Trump administration to wring some pretty stunning concessions from institutions that traditionally have prided themselves on their independence.
sentences.zh: 让特朗普政府能够从那些传统上以独立为荣的机构中榨取一些相当惊人的让步。

sentences.en: And I wonder how the people that you are talking to within academia are viewing what's happening to them within this broader context.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你所交谈的学术界人士是如何在更广泛的背景下看待发生在他们身上的事情的。

sentences.en: Well, there's a long history in the world of authoritarian regimes trying to pressure universities and transform them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，世界上有很长的历史，威权政权试图向大学施压并改造它们。

sentences.en: And there are some people in academia who feel these last few months have been at least steps toward that kind of reality.
sentences.zh: 学术界有些人觉得过去这几个月至少是迈向那种现实的步骤。

sentences.en: They see these steps as out of a strongman playbook.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这些步骤是强人政治剧本中的一部分。

sentences.en: You know, there was a book a couple years ago by the president of Johns Hopkins called What Universities Ode Democracy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，几年前约翰霍普金斯大学校长写过一本书，叫《大学欠民主什么》。

sentences.en: And he talked about in that book how the fate of universities and liberal democracies are entwined with one another.
sentences.zh: 他在书中谈到了大学的命运与自由民主的命运是如何交织在一起的。

sentences.en: So, you know, there are people in academia who are giving voice to these types of things.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，学术界有人在表达这些观点。

sentences.en: There was a statement last week from a center at Georgetown University that talked about kind of an encroaching authoritarianism by the administration.
sentences.zh: 上周乔治城大学的一个中心发表了一份声明，谈到了政府正在侵蚀威权主义。

sentences.en: You know, throwing out words like McCarthyism.
sentences.zh: 你知道，抛出像“麦卡锡主义”这样的词。

sentences.en: We keep hearing that word thrown around a lot.
sentences.zh: 我们一直听到这个词被频繁使用。

sentences.en: That kind of, you know, speech-suppressing, speech-chilling atmosphere is what people are trying to compare this moment to.
sentences.zh: 那种压制言论、令人寒蝉的氛围，正是人们试图用来比较当下时刻的东西。

sentences.en: On Saturday, I was talking with Mary Sue Coleman, who is a former president of the University of Michigan and the University of Iowa.
sentences.zh: 周六，我与密歇根大学和爱荷华大学的前校长 Mary Sue Coleman 进行了交谈。

sentences.en: And I was asking her, you know, what do you make of this decision by Columbia to concede what the administration wanted?
sentences.zh: 我问她，你如何看待哥伦比亚大学决定让步于政府想要的东西？

sentences.en: And her answer was pretty revealing.
sentences.zh: 她的回答相当发人深省。

sentences.en: And she said, I was alarmed by it because of what the ultimate consequences might be for higher education.
sentences.zh: 她说，我对此感到震惊，因为这最终可能会对高等教育产生什么后果。

sentences.en: But I don't want to say if I were sitting in their shoes that I would have made a different decision.
sentences.zh: 但我不想说如果我处在他们的位置，我会做出不同的决定。

sentences.en: Because these universities might have just calculated that it's just not worth fighting.
sentences.zh: 因为这些大学可能只是计算出，反抗根本不值得。

sentences.en: They don't stand a chance.
sentences.zh: 他们没有胜算。

sentences.en: I think some universities may very well decide it's an act of survival.
sentences.zh: 我认为一些大学很可能会决定这是一种生存行为。

sentences.en: And I think one of the biggest questions that's still out there is, what will the surviving university look like?
sentences.zh: 我认为目前最大的问题之一是，幸存下来的大学会是什么样子？

sentences.en: Will it be these places where research has flourished and there's been a lot of debate?
sentences.zh: 它会是那些研究繁荣、辩论激烈的地方吗？

sentences.en: Or will it be something different?
sentences.zh: 还是会变成别的东西？

sentences.en: And I think whatever the answer is, it's going to shape this country for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 我认为无论答案是什么，它都将长期塑造这个国家。

sentences.en: Alan, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: Alan，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是您今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Sunday, Canada's new prime minister, Mark Carney, called for a national election to take place next month on April 28th.
sentences.zh: 周日，加拿大新任总理马克·卡尼宣布将于下个月4月28日举行全国大选。

sentences.en: His liberal party is facing a strong challenge from the country's conservatives.
sentences.zh: 他的自由党正面临来自该国保守党的强力挑战。

sentences.en: And all of this comes at a turbulent time, as the Trump administration has imposed punishing tariffs and threatened the sovereignty of Canada, its neighbor and longtime ally.
sentences.zh: 这一切都发生在一个动荡的时期，特朗普政府不仅实施了惩罚性关税，还威胁到了其邻国兼长期盟友加拿大的主权。

sentences.en: And after weeks of pressure, Venezuela said it would resume accepting deportation flights from the United States.
sentences.zh: 在承受了数周的压力后，委内瑞拉表示将恢复接收来自美国的遣返航班。

sentences.en: This comes after the Trump administration invoked an obscure wartime law to deport Venezuelans accused of gang affiliations to El Salvador with little or no due process.
sentences.zh: 此前，特朗普政府援引了一项鲜为人知的战时法律，在几乎没有或完全没有正当程序的情况下，将涉嫌参与帮派活动的委内瑞拉人驱逐到了萨尔瓦多。

sentences.en: In a statement this weekend, a Venezuelan official said the country would not rest until we, quote, rescue our brothers kidnapped in El Salvador.
sentences.zh: 委内瑞拉官员在本周末的一份声明中表示，该国将“誓不罢休，直到我们救出被绑架在萨尔瓦多的兄弟们”。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Nina Feldman, Mooj Zadie, and Sidney Harper.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由尼娜·费尔德曼、穆杰·扎迪和西德尼·哈珀制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Patricia Willans with help from Ben Calhoun and M.J.
sentences.zh: 由帕特里夏·威兰斯编辑，本·卡尔霍恩和M.J.提供了协助。

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Marianne Lozano, Diane Wong, Rowan Nemisto, and Pat McCusker, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 包含玛丽安·洛萨诺、黛安·黄、罗文·内米斯托和帕特·麦卡斯克创作的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly乐队的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目中，我们将为您准备节日待客指南。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，了解如何让您的客人们宾至如归。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝断片了才去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 您可以在《纽约时报》应用程序或您喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《Wirecutter秀》。
